'''Gordon G. Hammes''' (born 1934 in [[Fond du Lac, Wisconsin]]) is a distinguished service professor of [[chemistry]], emeritus, at [[Duke University]], professor emeritus at [[Cornell University]], and member of [[United States National Academy of Sciences]]. Hammes' research involves the study of [[enzyme]] mechanisms and enzyme regulation.<ref name="ASBMBprofile">{{cite web|url=http://www.asbmb.org/uploadedfiles/aboutus/asbmb_history/past_presidents/1990s/1994Hammes.html|title=ASBMB Past Presidents|publisher=American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology|accessdate=3 May 2012|archive-date=5 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120605165924/http://www.asbmb.org/uploadedfiles/AboutUs/ASBMB_History/Past_Presidents/1990s/1994Hammes.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Hammes was born in [[Fond du Lac, Wisconsin]] in 1934. He earned his B.A. from [[Princeton University]] in 1956 and his Ph.D. from the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] in 1959.<ref name="ASBMBprofile"/>

==Career==
Hammes conducted postdoctoral research with [[Manfred Eigen]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry]] in [[Göttingen, Germany]]. He then secured a faculty position at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] before moving to [[Cornell University]] in 1965, where he was professor and chair of the department of chemistry.  At Cornell University, he was the Horace White Professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry, as well the director and co-founder of the Cornell University Biotechnology Program.  He spent some time at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] as vice-chancellor for academic affairs, and then joined the biochemistry faculty at Duke University in 1991.<ref name="ASBMBprofile"/> He served as vice chancellor of academic affairs at the Duke University Medical Center from 1991 through 1998.<ref name="Marchuk">{{cite web|url=http://mgm.duke.edu/news/marchuk.html |title=Marchuk Selected for 2010 Gordon G. Hammes Faculty Teaching Award |publisher=Duke Department of Molecular Genetics and Microbiology |accessdate=3 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111010113911/http://mgm.duke.edu/news/marchuk.html |archivedate=10 October 2011 }}</ref><ref name="DukeLibrary">{{cite web|url=http://archives.mc.duke.edu/mcahammesgg.html|title=Guide to the Gordon G. Hammes Papers and Records, 1987–2008|publisher=Duke Medical Center Library & Archives|accessdate=3 May 2012}}</ref>

Hammes was editor-in-chief of the [[American Chemical Society]] journal ''[[Biochemistry (journal)|Biochemistry]]'' from 1992 until 2003, and president of the [[American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology]] starting in 1994.<ref name="ASBMBprofile"/><ref name="NMC">{{cite web|url=http://www.naplesmusicclub.org/gordon-hammes/|title=Gordon Hammes|publisher=Naples Music Club|accessdate=3 May 2012}}</ref> The Gordon Hammes ACS Biochemistry Lectureship was established in 2009 in order to honor significant contributions to the field of biochemistry.<ref name="ACSdiv">{{cite web|url=http://www.divbiolchem.org/content/hammesawardees1.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216022831/http://www.divbiolchem.org/content/hammesawardees1.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 16, 2013|title=Gordon Hammes ACS Biochemistry Lectureship|publisher=American Chemical Society|accessdate=3 May 2012}}</ref>

===Research papers===
Dr. Hammes is a world leader in the field of enzyme mechanisms and regulation, starting with work with Eigen on the temperature-jump technique<ref name = "tj1">{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja01507a041| title= Kinetic Studies of ADP Reactions with the Temperature Jump Method| year= 1960| last1= Eigen| first1= Manfred| last2= Hammes| first2= Gordon G.| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society| volume= 82| issue= 22| pages= 5951–5952
| bibcode= 1960JAChS..82.5951E}}</ref><ref name = "tj2">{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja01473a056
| title= Kinetic Studies of ADP Reactions with the Temperature Jump Method—Corrections
| year= 1961
| last1= Eigen
| first1= Manfred
| last2= Hammes
| first2= Gordon G.
| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society
| volume= 83
| issue= 12
| page= 2786
| bibcode= 1961JAChS..83.2786E
}}</ref> and with [[Robert A. Alberty|Robert Alberty]] on diffusion-controlled reactions to enzyme kinetics. He studied the kinetic behavior of various enzymes, including glutamate-aspartate transaminase,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja00883a006
| title= A Kinetic Study of Glutamic-Aspartic Transaminase
| year= 1962
| last1= Hammes
| first1= Gordon G.
| last2= Fasella
| first2= Paolo.
| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society
| volume= 84
| issue= 24
| pages= 4644–4650
| bibcode= 1962JAChS..84.4644H
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/bi00865a026
| title= The Interaction of Aspartate Aminotransferase with α-Methylaspartic Acid
| year= 1966
| last1= Fasella
| first1= Paolo
| last2= Giartosio
| first2= Anna
| last3= Hammes
| first3= Gordon G.
| journal= Biochemistry
| volume= 5
| issue= 1
| pages= 197–202
| pmid= 5938937
}}</ref> hexokinase,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja00870a012
| title= Studies of the Enzyme Hexokinase. I. Steady State Kinetics at pH 8
| year= 1962
| last1= Hammes
| first1= Gordon G.
| last2= Kochavi
| first2= Daniel.
| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society
| volume= 84
| issue= 11
| pages= 2069–2073
| bibcode= 1962JAChS..84.2069H
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja00870a013
| title= Studies of the Enzyme Hexokinase. II. Kinetic Inhibition by Products
| year= 1962
| last1= Hammes
| first1= Gordon G.
| last2= Kochavi
| first2= Daniel.
| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society
| volume= 84
| issue= 11
| pages= 2073–2076
| bibcode= 1962JAChS..84.2073H
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja00870a014
| title= Studies of the Enzyme Hexokinase. III. The Role of the Metal Ion
| year= 1962
| last1= Hammes
| first1= Gordon G.
| last2= Kochavi
| first2= Daniel.
| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society
| volume= 84
| issue= 11
| pages= 2076–2079
| bibcode= 1962JAChS..84.2076H
}}</ref> and ribonuclease.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1002/bbpc.19640680818
| title= Relaxation Spectra of Ribonuclease
| year= 1964
| last1= Cathou
| first1= Renata E.
| last2= Hammes
| first2= Gordon G.
| journal= Berichte der Bunsengesellschaft für Physikalische Chemie
| volume= 68
| issue= 8–9
| pages= 759–760
}}</ref> He developed new methodologies that allowed a better understanding of enzyme catalysis,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/0005-2787(65)90094-8
| title= A Sephadex dialysis method of determining small molecule-macromolecule binding constants
| year= 1965
| last1= Fasella
| first1= Paolo
| last2= Hammes
| first2= Gordon G.
| last3= Schimmel
| first3= Paul R.
| journal= Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Nucleic Acids and Protein Synthesis
| volume= 103
| issue= 4
| pages= 708–710
| pmid= 5859855
}}</ref> including fast reaction techniques,<ref name = "tj1"/><ref name = "tj2"/> fluorescence spectroscopy, and single molecule microscopy.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1073/pnas.0700342104
| title= Single-molecule measurements of the opening and closing of the DNA gate by eukaryotic topoisomerase II
| year= 2007
| last1= Smiley
| first1= R. D.
| last2= Collins
| first2= T. R. L.
| last3= Hammes
| first3= G. G.
| last4= Hsieh
| first4= T.-S.
| journal= Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
| volume= 104
| issue= 12
| pages= 4840–4845
| pmid= 17360343
| pmc= 1829226
| bibcode= 2007PNAS..104.4840S
| doi-access= free
}}</ref><ref name="fret"/> He was also one of the first to develop fluorescence energy transfer (FRET) as a technology to study distances between and within proteins.<ref name="fret">{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/bi051378i
| title= Conformation Coupled Enzyme Catalysis: Single-Molecule and Transient Kinetics Investigation of Dihydrofolate Reductase
| year= 2005
| last1= Antikainen

| volume= 44
| issue= 51

| pmid= 16363797

===Books===

Books written by Hammes include the following:

::''Thermodynamics and Kinetics for the Biological Sciences'' (2000)<ref>{{cite book| isbn= 0-471-37491-1 | title = Thermodynamics and Kinetics for the Biological Sciences | last1= Hammes| first1= Gordon G.| date= 2000 | publisher = Wiley-Interscience | place = New York}}</ref>

::''Spectroscopy for the Biological Sciences'' (2005)<ref>{{cite book| isbn= 978-0471713449| title= Spectroscopy for the Biological Sciences| last1= Hammes| first1= Gordon G.| date= 2005| publisher= Wiley}}</ref>

::''Physical Chemistry for the Biological Sciences'' (2015) with his daughter [[Sharon Hammes-Schiffer]]<ref>{{cite book| isbn= 978-1118859001| title= Physical Chemistry for the Biological Sciences| last1= Hammes| first1= Gordon G.| last2= Hammes-Schiffer| first2= Sharon| date = 2015| publisher= John Wiley & Sons}}</ref>

==Awards and distinctions==
*1956 – McKay Prize in Chemistry<ref name="ASBMBprofile"/>
*1967 – American Chemical Society Award in Biological Chemistry<ref name="ASBMBprofile"/>
*1967 – [[Eli Lilly Award in Biological Chemistry]]
*2002 – American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology [[William C. Rose Award]]<ref name="ASBMBprofile"/>
*2008 – American Chemical Society Biochemistry Lectureship, Scholarship Award created in 2016
*2009 – Vallee Foundation board of directors
